lines: Morgan Kim
+1 (555) 010-8173 | morgan.kim@example.com | example.com/code/mkim
EDUCATION
Clearwater Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2017 - May 2021
EXPERIENCE
Northside Bakery | Delivery Driver | Metro City, USA | Aug 2025 - Present
- Delivered morning wholesale orders to about 20 cafés and collected signed invoices.
- Loaded the van and checked each order against the dispatch list before leaving.
Clearwater Sensors | Hardware Test Engineer | Metro City, USA | Jul 2021 - Feb 2023
- Owned the end-of-line test station for the humidity sensor and the yield reports the line leads used.
- Traced a batch of early field failures to a solder-paste change; the findings updated the reflow profile and cut returns from 2.1% to 0.4%.
- Wrote the calibration procedure for the sensor line, cutting calibration drift complaints from 15 to 2 a quarter.
- Designed a test fixture that checked 8 boards at once, raising station throughput from 40 to 150 boards an hour.
Voltline Robotics | Embedded Software Engineer | Metro City, USA | Mar 2023 - Jun 2025
- Improved update speed by 60% by compressing firmware images and resuming interrupted downloads.
- Wrote a hardware-in-the-loop test rig that ran 400 motor-control tests on every firmware build.
- Added a crash logger that saved the last 2 seconds of sensor data to flash, which found the root cause of 5 field failures.
- Sampled the motor's 5 kHz vibration signal at 8 kHz so the fault detector could capture it without aliasing.
- Fixed a race condition on the counter shared by the interrupt handler and the main loop by declaring the counter volatile.
- Rewrote the motor-controller firmware for a warehouse robot fleet of 300 units, cutting control-loop jitter from 120 to 15 microseconds and field motor faults by 60%.
PROJECTS
Low-Power Weather Station | Independent Project | C, STM32 | Jan 2025 - Present
- Built a solar-powered weather station on an STM32 that reports every 5 minutes over LoRa and runs 9 days without sun.
- Cut average current from 4.2 mA to 0.9 mA by sleeping between readings and batching radio transmissions.
- Published the schematics and firmware openly, and a local school built two stations from them.
Formula Student Electric Car | Electronics Lead, Team of 12 | C | Sep 2019 - May 2021
- Worked on firmware and testing for the robot fleet's motor controllers.
- Wrote the CAN-bus firmware for the dashboard and tested it against the motor controller before each race.
- Rewrote motor-control firmware for a fleet of about 300 robots, cutting control-loop jitter eightfold and motor faults by more than half.
SKILLS
Tools: C, C++, STM32, osciloscopes
Methods: firmware, hardware-in-the-loop testing, CAN, low-power design

items.says: Make the code link point directly to work an employer should see.
Make sure the code link is clickable in the submitted PDF.
Move Voltline Robotics above Clearwater Sensors.
items.because: The roles should continue in reverse chronological order after Northside Bakery.

items.says: Fix the character-encoding error in “cafØs.”
items.because: It looks like a PDF or text-export problem.

items.says: Specify the scale or outcome of the yield reporting.
items.because: “Owned” describes responsibility, but the reader cannot gauge its impact.

items.says: Clarify the period over which returns fell.
items.because: It would make the result easier to assess.

items.says: Clarify your role in confirming the solder-paste cause.
items.because: It would make the result easier to assess.

items.says: Define what counted as a drift complaint.
items.because: Otherwise, the reduction may look imprecise.

items.says: Give the comparison periods for the drift complaints, if possible.
items.because: Otherwise, the reduction may look imprecise.

items.says: Say whether “update speed” means download time, installation time, or end-to-end completion.
items.because: The percentage is ambiguous without that measure.

items.says: Add a reliability or release benefit if you have a defensible measure.
Say the crash logger helped identify the causes of five failures, rather than found them itself.
items.because: That distinction makes your contribution more precise.

items.says: Sampling a 5 kHz signal at 8 kHz does not, by itself, capture it without aliasing.
items.because: The Nyquist rate would be above 10 kHz.

items.says: Declaring the shared counter `volatile` does not, by itself, fix a race condition.
items.because: It does not make access atomic.

items.says: Check that the 60% reduction refers specifically to motor faults.
Check that the comparison period supports the fault-reduction claim.
Clarify the conditions behind “9 days without sun,” such as battery size or test setup.
items.because: That would make the endurance claim credible.

items.says: Check that “Electronics Lead” accurately describes your role.
Make your Formula Student leadership contribution visible in the bullets if you were Electronics Lead.
Remove or replace the robot-fleet firmware bullet.
items.because: It appears unrelated to a student electric car and overlaps with the Voltline role.

items.says: Add a test result if you have one.
Remove the 300-robot-fleet achievement from the Formula Student project.
items.because: It duplicates the Voltline achievement with different figures, creating a serious credibility concern.

items.says: Correct the misspelling “osciloscopes.”
Separate programming languages, platforms, and instruments.
items.because: They are currently grouped under one label.

items.says: List only methods you can discuss in depth.
Consider using the space for specific embedded tools or protocols not named elsewhere.
